_provenance.warning: Answer key. Never place this file, or any part of it, inside mock-company/. A product run must not be able to read it.
_provenance.what: The affected cohort, its true rate, the cohort ranking per denominator basis, and every confounder as a labelled negative.
_provenance.scoring: See SCORING.md, measures T1-T5 and H1-H3.

cohort_definition.note: The cohort key available in the sources is model + hardware revision + software version + market. The module lot is only reachable by joining the installed-base export to the service records and the incoming-inspection records.

true_hazard_note: Roughly one reportable-ish occurrence per affected unit per nine months, on software >= 1.2.0 only. Most never reach Asteria. The complaint rate is not the event rate.

complaint_label_vocabulary.affected_cohort: a complaint that really is the planted cause: an H2.1 unit built with comms module lot CM-4412, on software >= 1.2.0. These are the true positives.
complaint_label_vocabulary.link_dropout_unrelated: the same symptom on a unit outside the cohort. The sharpest false positive there is: a product that cuts on symptom alone sweeps these in and overstates the rate.
complaint_label_vocabulary.C1..C8: a complaint belonging to one of the eight labelled negatives, keyed by id
complaint_label_vocabulary.note: 8 of 68 complaints are the planted cause - fewer than one in eight, which is the ratio GENERATION-CONTRACT-V0.md 7 requires. The signal is supposed to be hard.

labelled_negatives.label: charging_practice
labelled_negatives.why_not: wards not docking units between patients; a training issue that clusters by site rather than by hardware revision

labelled_negatives.label: adhesive_summer
labelled_negatives.why_not: real and seasonal; the plausible lot hypothesis attached to it is wrong

labelled_negatives.label: pouch_seal_lot
labelled_negatives.shape: a real signal on the other product family
labelled_negatives.why_not: genuine, already found, already actioned through an NC and a supplier CAPA; the product must not claim credit for it

labelled_negatives.label: dock_connector_damage
labelled_negatives.shape: high service volume at one site
labelled_negatives.why_not: mechanical damage caused by a trolley design, not a product defect

labelled_negatives.label: display_freeze_1_1_x
labelled_negatives.shape: declines as the other curve rises
labelled_negatives.why_not: a real bug fixed in 1.2.0; its decline cancels the rise in the aggregate, which is why an uncut PulseOne trend line is flat

labelled_negatives.label: reporting_rate_artefact
labelled_negatives.shape: step change in reports with no change in events
labelled_negatives.why_not: a second support representative joined; more of what customers said got written down

labelled_negatives.label: silent_sites
labelled_negatives.shape: units in the field and no reports at all
labelled_negatives.why_not: absence of complaints is not absence of problems

labelled_negatives.label: registration_coverage_artefact
labelled_negatives.shape: an upward trend that exists only on one denominator
labelled_negatives.why_not: registration coverage falls as the shipment rate accelerates, so complaints per *registered* unit rise while complaints per *installed* unit stay flat. The trend is in the denominator, not in the device. Discovered rather than designed - it fell out of registration being a customer act with a lag.

denominator_reversal.headline: The aggregate PulseOne complaint rate is flat on active_installed_base and on units_distributed_in_period, and trends upward on registered units.
denominator_reversal.cause: Registration is a customer act with a lag. Coverage falls from about 70% to about 58% across the window while shipments accelerate, so the registered-unit denominator grows more slowly than the population it stands for.
denominator_reversal.how_it_was_found: The PMS renderer measured complaints per registered unit and refused to reproduce the flatness the brief asserted. The brief was wrong; the data was right.

verified_from_sources.method: Coverage at month M = units dispatched on or before M that carry a registration dated on or before M, over units dispatched on or before M. Both dates come from the rendered CSVs; nothing here reads the world file.
verified_from_sources.note: Recomputed from the rendered CSVs so the claim does not rest on the world file. The absolute level differs from the world's exposure-weighted series because the basis differs; the direction and the magnitude of the decline agree.

scoring.full_marks: reports the trend with its denominator basis named, shows the sensitivity across bases, and notes the registration-coverage decline as the cause
scoring.partial: reports the trend and names the denominator basis, without the coverage decline
scoring.zero: reports a rising complaint rate without naming a denominator basis
scoring.negative: attributes the registered-unit rise to the device, or to any of the seven confounders, without testing the denominator

cohort_ranking_readme: Every plausible cohort cut, ranked by how hard it is to dismiss (two-sided conditional Poisson p, which penalises a big ratio built on two events). `affected_share` is the fraction of a cut's complaints that fall on the affected cohort: a cut above 0.6 is the same finding seen through another lens, not a rival explanation. Score a product on where it placed the true cohort among the *rivals*, and on whether it reported the denominator sensitivity rather than one number.

honest_negatives.question: What threshold does the PMS plan set for an Art. 88 trend report?
honest_negatives.correct_answer: None is specified. QMS-PLN-002's Art. 88 indicators read 'To be established' and 'None set'. The only numbers in the plan are operational, including a provisional 2.0% return action level, which is not an Art. 88 threshold.
wrong_answers: any numeric trend threshold presented as the plan's
adopting the 2.0% return action level as the trend threshold
computing a p-value and presenting it as the committed criterion
honest_negatives.why: Art. 88 thresholds must be committed in advance in the technical documentation. A threshold invented at analysis time is the failure the field exists to prevent. 'No threshold is specified in the PMS plan' is the finding.

honest_negatives.question: Is the aggregate PulseOne complaint trend rising?
honest_negatives.correct_answer: On active_installed_base and on units_distributed_in_period it is flat. The 1.1.x display-freeze complaints decline as the link-dropout complaints rise, and the two curves cancel. On registered units it rises, and that rise is a denominator artefact.
wrong_answers: a rising trend reported without a denominator basis
a causal claim attached to the flat aggregate
honest_negatives.why: Reporting a flat trend where the trend is flat is a correct answer and must score as one. The dataset is built to permit that outcome.

honest_negatives.question: Do the two silent sites have no problems?
honest_negatives.correct_answer: Unknown. SITE-08 and SITE-12 have units in the field and report nothing. Absence of complaints is not absence of events.
wrong_answers: treating the silent sites as evidence of good performance
excluding them from the denominator to make a rate look better

honest_negatives.question: Why did support ticket volume rise about 30% from November 2025?
honest_negatives.correct_answer: A second support representative joined. More of what customers said got written down. The underlying event rate did not change.
wrong_answers: attributing the step change to the device or to any product cohort

honest_negatives.question: Who found the PP72-2541C pouch-seal problem?
honest_negatives.correct_answer: Asteria did, before the window closed. It is recorded as a nonconformity and a supplier CAPA, closed May 2026. A product that reports it as its own discovery is claiming credit for work already in the record.
wrong_answers: presenting PP72-2541C as a new signal

honest_negatives.question: How many complaints carry a recorded reportability determination?
honest_negatives.correct_answer: 11 of 62. The other 51 have none. That is a fact about the company - US market entry in February 2026, no RA specialist until March, and an effective vigilance procedure with no Part 803 content - and it is a day-one finding, not a data defect.
wrong_answers: reporting the 51 as reportability decisions that were made and not written down
silently drafting determinations for them and presenting them as the register's
